Own the index and provenance, not duplicate diagnoses or measurements. Preserve ECG, catheterization, surgery, medication history and functional status.

profiles.reason: Shared familial cardiology context; preserve variant interpretation, counseling, family screening and disease-specific panels.
Named SCID/CVID/IgA/CGD conditions plus suspected/confirmed, genetic, infection, malignancy and treatment contexts remain represented.
One respiratory index preserves bronchoscopy, genetics, oxygen, admissions, ventilatory support and outcomes with source versions.
Digestive index retains growth, histology, nutrition, procedure/outcome and imaging references without creating duplicate clinical truth.
The hematology index preserves CBC/coagulation, smear/marrow, genetic, transfusion, complication and outcome references with correction/version history.

Genetic report/reference profile preserves phenotype, variant/classification, family/carrier/pedigree and molecular assay context. Data indexing does not take over laboratory or genetics-review authority.

Tumor timeline preserves first symptoms, diagnostic delay/milestones, histology/molecular classification versions, stage/risk systems, recurrence and outcomes. TNM is a historical source label, not a universal pediatric staging system.

Case/procedure index owns authorized versioned references and chronology, not a second surgical/pathology/device truth store. Preserve surgical team, anatomical site, preoperative status and reoperation/outcome context.

Admission/birth index retains delivery details, initial exam, gestational age, birth weight, timed Apgar assessments and NICU course. Unknown birth times/identity are explicit; no retrospective score inference.
Authorized neonatal dataset index preserves imaging/lab/genetics, NICU, development/growth and longitudinal outcomes while research and model-training release gates remain separate.

Shunts, neurostimulators and intrathecal/other implants share one lifecycle owner with distinct device profiles. Preserve manufacturer/model, anatomical configuration, current versus historical settings, programming/revision, battery/explantation and exact imaging-compatibility evidence. Read access cannot issue device commands.

Intracranial/multimodal and intraoperative acquisition are separate device-channel profiles with units, clocks, signal quality, baseline/change/recovery and anesthesia/intervention correlation. Qualified real-time clinical monitoring is not replaced by recorded signals or AI.

Surgical and orthopedic implants share device lifecycle ownership. Preserve manufacturer/model/serial/lot when available, location, implantation/revision/removal/replacement, follow-up and imaging context. Missing identifiers remain unknown; recall surveillance needs authoritative source and acknowledged response, and MRI context is not compatibility approval.

Orthoses, prostheses, wheelchairs/walkers/standing/seating and communication/environmental aids are profiles of shared device lifecycle. Preserve needs/prescription, fitting, growth adjustment, skin/comfort, maintenance/replacement, use and functional goals; prescription authority stays clinical and device data does not authorize control.

Robotic/exoskeleton and gait/upper-limb devices retain prescription/protocol references, settings, session/adverse-event links, baseline, progress and maintenance. Encounter services own therapy delivery; source integration is read-only and does not program devices or select treatment intensity. The bounded configuration schema is not a complete robotics contract.
Assessment, protective factors, escalation, emergency disposition and follow-up remain human-led; preserve explicit prohibition of autonomous risk determination.

Suspected shunt malfunction uses current verified configuration and baseline/history to support urgent clinical assessment. Neither a model result nor missing data may delay evaluation or exclude malfunction.

Preserve initial stabilization, timed airway/compression/oxygen/administration and outcome documentation. Guideline intent requires a named approved version and qualified team; the system does not generate or autonomously execute resuscitation instructions.

Shared emergency records retain fever, seizures, trauma, poisoning/admissions, dehydration, respiratory failure and pediatric resuscitation scope. A registry is not an emergency dispatch or autonomous triage service.

Eye emergency profiles retain acute vision loss, chemical burns, globe/orbital/corneal/anterior/posterior injury, laterality/time and visual recovery; diagrams do not require delaying urgent care for imaging.

Airway obstruction/foreign body and odontogenic spread are distinct emergency profiles sharing human escalation. Preserve dental origin, drainage/extraction/referral and antibiotic history without automated exclusion or prescribing.
Severe skin/allergic emergency profile preserves named SJS/TEN and severe-reaction scope; no model-only diagnosis or unsupervised medication action.

Acute abdomen/obstruction/trauma and ovarian/testicular emergencies retain different anatomy, laterality, onset, viability/preservation and procedural contexts. Automated systems cannot rule out torsion or delay specialist assessment.
Individualized allergy/anaphylaxis plan preserves clinician/version, trigger/medication instruction, caregiver/school minimal scope and emergency contacts; sharing never creates a new prescription.

Prehospital transfer retains injury/transport chronology, interventions, sending/receiving identities and handover acknowledgement with time/source uncertainty. Cross-provider transport does not grant broad passport access.
Retain corrective/palliative surgery, valve and great-vessel detail, hospital/surgeon identity and imaging follow-up. AI does not authorize surgery.
profiles.workflow: Preoperative assessment → authorized plan → procedure documentation → postoperative/ICU follow-up → longitudinal outcomes.

Retain capsule/endoscopic ultrasound, therapeutic interventions, images, biopsy location, sedation and complications; image AI is a referenced task.
Preserve baseline, gait/balance, range of motion, assistive devices, OT/PT/home plan and agreed activity goals.

The marrow procedure profile preserves aspiration/core biopsy, specimen tracking, morphology/cellularity, flow, cytogenetic/molecular and signed pathology references. Procedure and laboratory interpretation authorities remain separate.

Apheresis is a procedure/session profile of the existing encounter owner. Preserve access, machine, replacement fluid, anticoagulation, collection product and complications without enabling device control.
Radiotherapy/proton course profiles distinguish planned and delivered dose, fractionation, cranial/spinal targets, critical structures and lifetime exposure; no treatment-equipment control.
Retain operative indication, margins, extent-of-resection assessment, postoperative MRI, pathology, CSF/neurological complications and adjuvant context.

Neurosurgical tumor procedures complement the existing oncologic surgery profile. Preserve intraoperative findings, molecular/pathology links, residual/extent-of-resection assessment, postoperative imaging and CSF/neurological outcomes.

Surgical planning is a versioned encounter workflow linking registered imaging/navigation, functional/vascular anatomy, neurophysiology/anesthesia/blood/device plans and final signed plan; no navigation accuracy claim is inferred.

Neuroendoscopic procedure profile retains indication/ETV type, preoperative and intraoperative findings, procedure date, CSF dynamics, complications, failure, repeat procedures and shunt conversion with clinician outcome assessment.

Postoperative recovery documentation retains baseline/current neurological status, wound/device, swallowing/speech, functional goals, rehabilitation and school reintegration as a profile of shared encounter follow-up.
Postoperative pediatric ICU is an encounter/history profile retaining ventilation, monitoring, complications and outcomes, not evidence that every ICU function is implemented.

Surgical and orthopedic perioperative records share procedure ownership. Preserve procedure/date/surgeon/outcome, trauma ICU and rehabilitation, laparoscopic versus thoracoscopic equipment, indication, imaging plan, consent, anesthesia, blood loss, implants and postoperative wound/mobility context. Clinical indication and anesthetic authorization remain separate signed decisions.

Rehabilitation plans retain clinician-approved physiotherapy/nutrition/activity, functional baseline, strength/motion/gait/balance, sessions, home goals, occupational therapy and discharge. Return-to-school and activity are distinct decisions; completion of an exercise does not imply clearance.

Return-to-learn, daily activity, PE, training and sport are separately scoped clinician decisions with baseline/function, symptoms, restrictions, testing and review date. Record progression and clearance independently; no single approval automatically grants the other scopes.

Occupational and speech/language/swallowing sessions retain distinct goals, clinician, fine-motor/self-care/feeding/handwriting/environment and voice/alternative communication/feeding-safety context. Shared therapy record ownership preserves specialty differences; exercises do not establish safe oral feeding.
Preserve Doppler, valve/chamber/ventricular/congenital assessment and source images/reports. AI image interpretation is separately governed.

Retain all CBC indices, differential/reticulocytes, age-adjusted reference context, acute-illness baseline, factor/inhibitor/mixing studies, anticoagulant and hepatic context. Assay results remain source-owned observations, not diagnoses.

IVIG/SCIG therapy shares product/route/exposure tracking; retain biological therapy as a separate subtype, infusion reactions, home care and product changes.

Exposure/regimen records preserve intent, protocol/cycle/day, weight/BSA context, prerequisites, delays, modifications and completion/discontinuation. Prescription and administration services retain authority.
Neonatal antibiotic, nutrition and infusion exposure shares medication ownership with distinct route/units/time/status; prescribing and administration retain separate authority.
Preserve renal/genetic/pathology/imaging/dialysis/transplant history, emergency context and cross-border language support. Export alone is not completed handover.

profiles.reason: Current authorized blood passport and adult handover preserve antibodies/factor/inhibitor context, emergency plan and specialist contact; receipt and acceptance remain separate from export and from blood-bank release.

Cancer exposure passport is a profile of existing passport ownership, retaining original/molecular diagnosis, surgery, chemotherapy, radiation, cellular therapy, transplant and late-effect surveillance history.

Neurosurgical and dental/craniofacial emergency views share passport ownership with specialty profiles. Preserve current device configuration, placement/removal/replacement, critical medications, bleeding/immunosuppression and communication needs; underlying device records stay authoritative.

Orthopedic adult handover preserves major diagnoses/injuries/operations, current implants/prostheses/aids, medication/allergy, imaging, function and rehab timeline. Multilingual and cross-border views reference verified source versions and purpose-specific consent, not unrestricted disclosure.

Retain mortality/morbidity, agency-specific reporting, cohorts, imaging datasets and neurosurgical outcomes. Research education is not cohort processing; anonymous wording needs disclosure validation.

Discovery/matching and actual investigational enrollment are distinct research profiles. Preserve site-verified criteria, trial/protocol/consent versions, treatment arm, deviations, adverse events and withdrawal.
Prematurity, respiratory/nutrition and ICU study profiles retain separate protocol/data-release and training permissions; AI dataset intent is not approval.

Recovery time, quality of life, long-term outcomes, procedure counts, complications and AI forecasts are distinct analytic measures. Preserve denominators, follow-up windows, missingness and model provenance; analytic inclusion requires authorized purpose and forecasts do not establish causal effectiveness.
3061 retains ICU and lifelong follow-up; 3661 adds hypertension/prevention/electrophysiology; 4061 emphasizes ECG/MRI. One profile retains each scope.
Retain specific defect names, single-ventricle physiology, hemodynamics, procedures and explicit adult-congenital transition.
Retain named channelopathies, AV/conduction disorders, bradyarrhythmia, Holter/event monitoring and electrophysiology.
Symptoms, myocarditis, mechanical support, fluid status, hospitalization, transplant evaluation and function are complementary.
Workspace and coordination views share data but retain rehabilitation, research, genetics and ICU interfaces.
Dashboard, clinical core and orchestration layers differ; no duplicate patient stores or mandatory deployment-per-module inference.
Retain broad clinical domains plus explicit episode/assessment schema and workflows; local MVP wording does not expand EDHT P0.
Retain developmental/substance/family care, restricted summaries, passport and conditional adult transfer; no universal guardian or school access.
Retain allergy dashboard, immune integration, vaccine clearance, anaphylaxis, immunotherapy and transition across shared owners.
5002 extends baseline/recovery and multisystem phenotype; retain explicit vaccine-response and test-type detail from 4444.
Combined-immunity scope and neonatal SCID screening require linked but distinct screening, confirmation, escalation and definitive-treatment states.
Respiratory orchestration retains congenital/airway/rare disease, sleep, home ventilation and emergency/passport interfaces. A common workspace delegates clinical facts and orders to their owners.
Asthma profiles distinguish diagnosis, control, exacerbation, trigger inference, allergic context and signed action plan. Preserve biologics, age-appropriate framework and school disclosure.

CF shares a longitudinal profile while retaining CFTR-modulator eligibility, pancreatic/nutrition/endocrine/fertility context and exacerbation recovery. Molecular interpretation and medication orders remain separate.
Digestive orchestration preserves hepatology, pancreatic/motility/feeding/intestinal-failure care and nutrition with shared source owners and separate signed plans.

Retain IBD-unclassified/indeterminate terminology history, Crohn location/behavior, UC extent, monogenic immune context, growth and instrument-specific activity; no automatic scores or targeted treatment.
Retain named functional disorders and legacy Rome IV reference, evolving framework version, motility testing, continence and patient-reported burden.

Nutrition profiles retain feeding skills, micronutrients, formula/route and fluid/calorie units, PN composition/access, remaining bowel anatomy and adaptation. Orders and pump/compounding actions remain external authorized workflows.
Systemic disease orchestration retains all organ interfaces, specialty independence, evolving phenotype and adult handover; local MVP wording does not change global adult P0.
Retain subtype, active/limited joint counts, intra-articular procedure history, uveitis and growth, plans and guardian diaries.
One examination/map profile preserves laterality, effusion, tendon involvement, injection/surgery history, gait and observed versus rendered findings.
Systemic and renal lupus assessments are coordinated profiles; retain urinary/blood-pressure/biopsy/complement evidence, organ damage and renal relapse with separate clinical authority.
Preserve electrophysiology, muscle biopsy, swallowing/respiratory involvement, calcinosis and multidisciplinary rehabilitation.
Localized and systemic scope retains vascular/skin distribution, contracture, organ surveillance and change timeline without collapsing disease classifications.
Preserve vessel distribution/size, ocular and other organ contexts, biopsy, damage and recurrence.
Maintain diagnostic classification history and uncertain/evolving overlap phenotype; normalization never forces a diagnosis.
Keep patient/guardian attribution, school and social participation, sleep/fatigue and treatment burden even when inflammatory markers are normal.

One hematology orchestration profile retains hemostasis, marrow failure, apheresis, hemovigilance, immune/genetic interfaces and adult transition. It delegates authoritative results, blood-bank releases and treatment orders.

Retain anemia subtypes, reticulocyte response, iron/vitamin/renal/inflammatory context, oral/IV iron history and menstrual/GI blood loss as distinct clinical contexts; no automatic diagnosis or iron prescription.

Sickle-cell and thalassemia remain distinct disease profiles sharing longitudinal infrastructure. Retain carrier/newborn screening, acute chest/stroke/splenic risk, hydroxyurea context, alloantibodies, MRI iron, chelation and endocrine/bone outcomes.

Preserve hemophilia, von Willebrand and rare factor/fibrinogen/platelet-function disorders separately; inhibitor and non-factor therapy, home treatment, dental/surgery and menstrual bleeding context remain explicit.

Platelet/white-cell/multilineage marrow profiles retain qualitative platelet disease, cyclic neutropenia, named inherited syndromes, medication/toxin exposure, prophylaxis and transplant evaluation without equating every cytopenia.

HSCT coordination retains donor search/HLA, conditioning, engraftment, GVHD, immune recovery and lifelong complications. Donor identity/permissions are separate, and no matching score determines eligibility.
Venous/arterial/catheter/cerebral events, provoking factors, recurrence, post-thrombotic outcomes and genetic/acquired risk remain distinct; testing and anticoagulation decisions are specialist-led.

Oncology and CNS-specific orchestration are profiles of the shared specialty owner. Preserve tumor-specific interfaces, molecular evolution, rehabilitation, palliative and lifelong developmental care without fragmenting source records.

Multidisciplinary diagnostic integration retains specimen/surgical source, DNA/RNA/epigenetic context, lab/pathologist/report versions, external review and tumor-board evidence. Signed pathology and reclassification remain attributable.
ALL/AML/mixed-lineage profiles retain immunophenotype, cytogenetic/molecular risk, treatment phases and MRD assay/time-point/sensitivity context; missing MRD never implies remission.

Distinct glioma/embryonal/ependymal/sellar/optic-pathway tumor profiles retain molecular grouping, CSF/spinal staging, resection, endocrine/visual function and supportive care; stable imaging cannot erase visual decline.

Response, recurrence, toxicity and survivorship profiles retain criterion/version, discordant modalities, repeat molecular/biopsy evidence, cumulative exposure, secondary malignancy and lifelong follow-up; no invented schedule.

Educational communication and concurrent palliative/supportive care are separate specialty workflows. Preserve age-appropriate multilingual explanation, symptoms, care goals and family needs without implying treatment cessation.

Keep seizures/neurological deficits, endocrine/water-balance/growth, cognitive baseline, educational accommodations and hearing/vision outcomes as linked profiles with source attribution and minimum-necessary school disclosure.

CAR-T coordination uses a specialty profile and existing source owners; retain chain of identity/custody through collection, manufacturing, bridging, release and infusion. Manufacturing progress is not product-release authority.

Shared neurosurgical orchestration retains prenatal-to-adult scope, neuroendoscopy, neurotrauma, surgical planning, implants, neurocritical care and rehabilitation. Independent deployability remains an option; AI cannot determine indication or operative strategy.

Hydrocephalus and tumor-related CSF disease are clinical coordination profiles. Preserve ventricular/head-growth/development/vision, CSF diversion, external drainage/ETV and infection/revision context; actual device configuration stays with the device owner.
Preserve suture/syndromic phenotype, functional/cosmetic outcomes, airway/ophthalmic/neurodevelopment and dental/orthodontic reconstruction context within one craniofacial profile.

Neural-tube and other congenital disorders retain prenatal linkage, lesion level/closure, motor/sensory, kidney/bladder/bowel, skin, nutrition, education and social care. Verified maternal-child linkage does not merge identities or permissions.
Retain malformation classification, brainstem/swallowing/sleep-breathing, syrinx, CSF-flow imaging, decompression complications and response surveillance.

Distinct syrinx, injury, tethering, dysraphism and spinal-tumor profiles retain anatomy/measurements, neurological and renal/urodynamic function, retethering, pathology and rehabilitation; they are not synonymous diagnoses.

Preserve treatment-failure history, video-EEG, functional/structural imaging, genetic/metabolic and neuropsychology context, surgical hypothesis, conference, consent and separately authorized decision; neither AI nor a test establishes eligibility alone.

Functional/spasticity/dystonia/pain/epilepsy therapy coordination retains goals, intrathecal therapy, implantation/programming history, battery and functional outcomes while device and medication owners retain their facts.

Neurovascular and intracranial-bleeding profiles retain AVM/cavernous/aneurysm/moyamoya, angiography, coagulation/anticoagulant/hemophilia context and endovascular/radiosurgical outcomes. No autonomous hemostatic or reversal action.

Severe injury and concussion retain mechanism/time, consciousness/amnesia, ICU/imaging and school/cognitive recovery. Return-to-learn and return-to-activity require distinct clinician clearance; a low automated risk signal cannot exclude acute injury.
Preserve wound/CNS/shunt infection, CSF leak/hemorrhage, microbiology/resistance, device removal/replacement, ICU/reoperation and attributable resolution versus suspected findings.

One neonatal orchestration owner coordinates delivery-room, term/preterm, ICU, congenital and lifelong developmental profiles. Maternal and infant records remain distinct, and historical local MVP claims do not authorize deployment.
Preserve extremely/very/moderate preterm contexts, growth, respiratory support, neurodevelopment and complication follow-up with appropriate age/reference applicability.

NICU coordination retains high-flow and high-frequency ventilation as distinct modalities alongside CPAP, hemodynamic monitoring, infection control and nutrition. Source observations and prescribed settings remain separate from control.
Keep transient tachypnea, distress, meconium aspiration, persistent pulmonary hypertension, BPD and apnea distinct with ventilation/oxygen history and clinical interpretation.
Early/late-onset and congenital infection/meningitis remain distinct episode contexts; microbiology, antibiotics and response retain source timing and clinical diagnosis authority.

Jaundice profile coordinates source bilirubin, age/gestation, phototherapy and separately authorized exchange-transfusion context. No thresholds or treatment recommendation are inferred from a legacy title.

Screening, confirmatory evaluation and established congenital diagnosis are distinct states. Preserve metabolic/hearing/cardiac, chromosomal/rare/genomic and organ-specific anomalies plus family counseling without treating a screen as diagnosis.

Preserve breastfeeding, donor milk, fortification, enteral/parenteral routes, tolerance and growth. Orders/formula changes and administration remain separately authorized; donor product provenance is not blanket donor access.

Growth/development and complications retain measurement time/technique, weight/length/head circumference and selected reference release. Historical WHO wording does not prove suitability for every gestational age.
Preserve reflex/tone examination, seizures, HIE, hemorrhage/leukomalacia and source neuroimaging without collapsing distinct injury phenotypes into a single AI label.
Cardiac neonatal profile links congenital diagnoses and echo/monitoring source data to specialist review using existing clinical/imaging/device owners.

Congenital malformations, appendicitis and hernia are separate specialty profiles. Preserve congenital imaging/follow-up, appendiceal histology/recovery and inguinal, umbilical and diaphragmatic anatomy without collapsing urgency or treatment pathways.

Wound infection, bleeding, sepsis, reoperation and recovery extend musculoskeletal infection profiles. Preserve osteomyelitis, septic arthritis, implant infection, aspiration, cultures/susceptibility, duration, response and recurrence. Suspected and confirmed episodes differ; prescribing remains with medication authority.

Surgical dashboard and orthopedic core/hub compose shared source-owned clinical services. Preserve examination, congenital/acquired disease, growth, hip/spine/limb/foot/hand, trauma, surgery, orthotics/prosthetics, pain, outcomes and MVP-versus-expansion scope. Modular deployment remains optional; local MVP labels do not authorize release.

Functional examination retains posture, gait, joint stability, range of motion, strength/tone, limb alignment/length, pain and device use with examiner/method/age. Baseline, growth and postoperative changes must remain distinguishable from model-generated trends.

Congenital orthopedics and skeletal dysplasia share longitudinal coordination with distinct genetic/phenotypic profiles. Preserve prenatal/neonatal context, proportions, craniofacial, respiratory and neurological associations, imaging/molecular provenance, casting/orthotics and adult transition without merging maternal identity or genetic consent.

Hip development, dysplasia and preservation retain laterality, screening/instability, imaging methods/measurements, gait, bracing/casting, surgery and skeletal-growth surveillance. Measurements require age/method context and never independently authorize surgery.

Scoliosis, kyphosis/lordosis and congenital, neuromuscular and syndromic deformity remain distinct profiles. Preserve curve method, source acquisition, maturity/growth, brace/physiotherapy and operative outcomes; incompatible images cannot substantiate progression automatically.

Limb discrepancy/deformity and growth-plate surveillance preserve length, rotation, mechanical axis, injury site/classification, growth arrest and serial correction context. Guided growth, lengthening, osteotomy and fixation remain specialist decisions; fracture healing does not close growth surveillance.

Foot/ankle and upper-extremity profiles retain separate anatomy: clubfoot/flatfoot/cavus/toes/instability versus congenital limb differences, shoulder/elbow/wrist/hand, strength and sensation. Preserve casting, recurrence, splints, orthotics, occupational therapy and functional outcomes.

Fracture/complex high-energy injury profiles preserve mechanism, dislocation, open fracture, pelvic/soft-tissue damage, neurovascular assessment, reduction, temporary stabilization and definitive fixation. Growth-plate/remodeling, healing, implant/wound/infection and return-to-activity context remain explicit; no automated injury exclusion.

Sports care retains athlete/training context, acute versus overuse and apophyseal/bone-stress injury, nutrition/endocrine associations, load modification, rehab, recurrence and functional tests. A recovery trajectory cannot issue return-to-sport permission.

Bone health preserves recurrent fracture/density, vitamin D/calcium/phosphate, genetic/endocrine/renal/nutritional context, medication and mobility. Lab results remain source-owned with units and age context; no universal pediatric treatment threshold is inferred.

Musculoskeletal oncology retains tumor anatomy, biopsy, histology/molecular evidence, staging reference, systemic treatment, resection/reconstruction, limb preservation, prosthesis and recurrence/function. This coordinates existing oncology and pathology authority rather than creating a second staging truth.

Acute/chronic/postoperative pain retains anatomical severity, sleep/school/function, medication, nonpharmacologic/psychological therapies and patient outcomes. Clinical medication and intervention decisions are distinct from tracking or inferred recovery.

Trauma core/polytrauma and recovery hub share orchestration across prehospital, multisystem organs, imaging/lab, procedures, ICU, blood products, sports and rehabilitation. One episode timeline preserves source-specific times and clinician prioritization. Independent services and future wearables/robotics/twin/research are retained without claiming implemented coverage.

Thoracic/abdominal profiles retain pulmonary/pleural/cardiac, liver/spleen/kidney/gastrointestinal/pancreatic/pelvic injury, monitoring, nonoperative, surgical and interventional contexts with attributable decisions; automated summaries never determine treatment priority.

Complex wounds and burns preserve location/tissue/contamination/neurovascular status, debridement/closure/reconstruction versus burn depth/extent, airway/fluid/graft context. Preserve infection/scar/contracture, pain, nutrition, psychological support and growth-related function; no unvalidated resuscitation instructions are generated.

Cardiorespiratory medical safety and nutrition are separate athlete health profiles. Preserve exercise symptoms/syncope/family history, specialist restrictions/emergency plan, growth/energy/iron/bone and menstrual context where appropriate. Health precedes performance; coach access does not authorize sensitive adolescent disclosures.

Rehabilitation coordination retains temporary/permanent impairment, mobility/strength/balance, daily living, cognition/communication/swallowing, goals, pain and school/home/social participation; it composes therapy-specific plans and source-owned devices.

Clinical motion assessment retains observational versus instrumented gait, kinematics/kinetics, muscle activity, speed/endurance, orthotic/surgical context and longitudinal comparison. Raw acquisition stays device-owned; methods, units, anatomical frame and calibration must be compatible before comparison or twin inference.

Functional outcomes preserve mobility/self-care/communication, school/social/recreation, sleep/pain/fatigue, independence and caregiver assistance. Patient and guardian reports retain respondent and instrument/version; proxy and patient perspectives remain distinct and missing values are not imputed independence.
Preserve family consultation, AI translation, ECG/echo review, home wearable/BP/heart-rate/symptom data. A connected device does not prove continuous clinical coverage.
profiles.workflow: Authorize consultation/monitoring scope → receive provenance-tagged reports → clinician review → acknowledgement/action → follow-up.

prior_contract.clinical_safety: No autonomous prescribing, dose change, device control or emergency disposition. Derived output cannot overwrite measured/observed facts; reviewed recommendations and clinical orders are separate.
prior_contract.privacy: Tenant, purpose, relationship, consent/assent, age, jurisdiction, expiry and revocation are checked per record/encounter. Restricted notes and family information are segmented; exports and caches inherit controls.
prior_contract.failure_modes: Wrong patient/unit/source version or revoked permission fails closed. Incomplete context returns an explicit limited/unknown result. Clinical care never waits for automated data completion. Communication failure is visible and requires the configured human escalation path.
prior_contract.acceptance: Preserve every source fragment, stable owner and exactly one alias per source. Reject stale versions, unknown identity/units, unauthorized disclosures and autonomous clinical writes. Verify idempotent events and correction history.
prior_contract.open_gates: Clinical intended-use approval, jurisdiction policy, terminology/profile releases, partner conformance, runtime security and numerical/model evaluation remain open. Documentation adoption does not close them.

profiles.reason: Preserve home spirometry, ventilator/oxygen review, medication supervision, translation and second opinion; do not equate consultation with monitored emergency coverage.
Nutrition/growth/lab/medication review, endoscopy discussion, translation and family counseling share a consultation workflow, not a feeding-prescription engine.

Remote consultation preserves bleeding/pain diaries, attributed home measurements, transfusion follow-up, laboratory review, translation and second opinion without assuming continuous emergency supervision.
Secure second-opinion/remote review preserves clinical questions and source imaging/pathology/genomics/treatment packages with translation and receiving-specialist access controls.
Remote follow-up preserves attributed guardian symptom/wound/device reports, approved instructions and escalation recipient/fallback; connection does not establish emergency coverage.
Regional NICU consultation, parent counseling, imaging and post-discharge follow-up retain provider coverage, source verification and translation limits.

Home orthopedic and rehabilitation follow-up retains cast/wound/device reports, pain/motion/activity/adherence, approved exercise plan, video review and program updates. Preserve respondent, source clock and validation; named escalation/fallback is required and connectivity does not prove emergency coverage.
Retain development, function, anatomy, hemodynamics, progression and surgical scenario models with explicit epistemic status.

Cardiac patient models retain anatomy/function/hemodynamics/development and surgical scenarios. Operational hospital/physician models are excluded from patient physiology and remain separate pending operational-owner review.

Organ development/growth models, therapy/NICU scenarios and long-term forecasts share twin infrastructure but remain separately typed hypothetical outputs, never measured development or clinical fact.

Previously reviewed growth and trauma twins become explicit shared-twin profiles. Preserve skeletal anatomy/axis/length/spine/muscle/joint versus preinjury neurological/mobility/pain/school baseline, injury/intervention/device/rehab and functional trajectories. Observed facts remain source-owned; scenario/model assumptions, uncertainty and versions are visible and clinician reviewed, never a treatment command.

User accounts, session/auth APIs and account-device trust share identity ownership, distinct from clinical patient records and medical-device acquisition. Preserve all account fields/endpoints, logout/revocation, recovery, MFA/passkey/biometric intent; implement token references/hashes and protected credential storage rather than exposed access_token/refresh_token columns. Profile editing never changes clinical authority.

Practitioner and organization records confirm ownership of pediatric surgeon/center profiles. Preserve qualifications, surgical specialization, languages, license/verification source, facilities/ICU/OR/contact and temporal role. Facility flags do not prove live availability, and licensure does not imply specific privileges.

Twelve specialty bookings and surgery booking are profiles of one appointment owner. Preserve each specialty, clinic, clinician/surgeon and online/telemedicine channel; booking is not a consultation encounter, consent or surgical authorization. Availability/reschedule/cancel and time-zone rules require bounded contract evidence.

Audit actions preserve actor/session/entity/result/security-investigation provenance. Raw old_value/new_value, IP and location legacy fields need minimized/redacted or encrypted-reference migration; never log bearer tokens or unrestricted health payloads. Compliance labels remain goals, not certifications.

Consent history and family access share policy ownership with explicit recipient, resource, purpose, expiry, withdrawal and guardian evidence. Family roles and signed/accepted flags do not prove legal authority. Preserve language/country/version/signature provenance while separating law/policy approval and access enforcement.

Core profile table/API becomes a source-linked projection with explicit unknowns, provenance and time. Preserve emergency card, summary/timeline/export, demographics, donor/disability/genetic/coverage references. Legacy mandatory blood-group/Rh fields must not force fabricated values; conditions/medication/allergies remain their owners facts.

QR session, role templates and access levels share scoped disclosure ownership. Preserve time/one-time/revocation/recipient and audit events, but public/full-record/permanent templates are not grants. Opaque token references, authenticated recipient/purpose and online revocation protect content; offline copies cannot promise immediate revocation.

Document metadata/storage/media and OCR are shared original/derivative lifecycle profiles. Preserve MIME/hash, source issue/expiry/provider, scan/quarantine, immutable originals, thumbnails, OCR/translation/model lineage and all legacy formats/features. Extracted dose/signature text is unverified; storage_path and signed URLs are not public record fields.

Notification records and templates share a delivery lifecycle owner with channel/version/language, preferences, schedule, priority and failure/retry states. Sent/read is not human acknowledgement. External payloads are redacted and tokens protected; emergency routing requires confirmed contracts and coverage.

Session records preserve appointment/actor/provider/link/time, translator/AI/recording choices, clinical note and prescription references. Recording and secondary use require independent permission; no public meeting URLs or implied emergency coverage.

SOS and emergency mode coordinate optional location/biometric, calls, contacts, offline view and scoped QR with acknowledged recipients. Source clinical facts stay separately owned; unknown/stale information and delivery failure remain visible. No unconditional hospital disclosure or autonomous diagnosis.

Doctor portal composes patient and encounter workflows, independently owned prescribing, appointments, documents and telemedicine. Preserve signature/credential/clinical role requirements and future dictation/integration features without treating portal access as universal patient or prescribing permission.

FHIR/HL7 and gateway profiles share translation/transport ownership. Preserve every listed resource/message/version/connector category and circuit-breaker/retry/audit requirement; each actual partner release needs schemas, terminology and loss fixtures. No automatic connector activation, unsupported conformance claim or clinical truth overwrite.

DICOM and PACS profiles share imaging ownership with original study/series/instance, acquisition, modality and diagnostic lineage. Preserve DIMSE/DICOMweb, vendor candidates and viewing capabilities while requiring partner validation and independently governed AI/anonymization.

LIS import preserves report/specimen/result, source units/method/reference range, correction history and critical-result delivery acknowledgement. HL7/FHIR/LOINC and other formats are candidate bindings; no unverified range conversion or autonomous clinical interpretation.

Medical wearable/home connector profiles retain listed brands, measured signals and source clocks/quality/pairing/consent with deduplication. Account trust devices remain identity-owned. RPM data paths do not authorize device commands, closed-loop treatment or emergency classification.

Anesthesia assistant is an explicit task profile retaining allergy, prior anesthetic, airway and interaction context; source/model versions, uncertainty and qualified validation are mandatory. No automatic selection, dosing or airway clearance.

Anesthesia and pre/intra/postoperative care are encounter profiles with clinical assessment, medication-plan references, source monitoring, recovery and enhanced-recovery protocol/version. AI risk prediction remains governed separately; no inferred thresholds or autonomous discharge.

ENT, dental behavioral/sedation, adolescent gynecologic and reconstructive urologic procedures retain distinct airway/hearing/implant, accommodation/adverse event, ovarian preservation/consent-assent, catheter/drain/stent/specimen and functional outcomes. Existing encounter owner coordinates source-owned device/pathology/medication; family access and clinical authority remain restricted.
